subject: general
question: Which of the following pigments is present in the red blood corpuscles of human beings?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Haemoglobin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Haemoglobin** is the iron-containing protein in red blood cells responsible for transporting oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body.
 
• Each haemoglobin molecule can bind up to four oxygen molecules, enabling efficient oxygen transport.
 
• Haemoglobin also plays a critical role in transporting carbon dioxide from tissues back to the lungs for exhalation.
 
• The presence of haemoglobin gives red blood cells their characteristic red color.
 
• Normal haemoglobin levels vary by age and sex, with adult males typically having 13.8 to 17.2 grams per deciliter and females having 12.1 to 15.1 grams per deciliter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Red Blood Cells (RBCs)**

 
 
• RBCs are the most common type of blood cell and the primary means of delivering oxygen to body tissues via blood flow.
 
• They are produced in the bone marrow and have a lifespan of about 120 days.
 
• RBCs are biconcave in shape, which increases their surface area for oxygen absorption.
 
• The average diameter of a human red blood cell is about 6-8 micrometers.
 
 
 
• **Oxygen Transport**
 
 
• Oxygen is carried in the blood bound to haemoglobin within red blood cells.
 
• Oxygen binds to the iron atoms in haemoglobin molecules in the lungs, forming oxyhaemoglobin.
 
• This oxygen is then released to tissues throughout the body where it is needed for cellular respiration.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Dioxide Transport**
 
 
• Carbon dioxide produced as a waste product of cellular respiration is transported back to the lungs in several forms.
 
• About 20-25% of CO2 is carried by haemoglobin as carbaminohaemoglobin.
 
• The majority of CO2 is converted to bicarbonate ions (HCO3-) in the blood plasma.
 
• In the lungs, CO2 is released from haemoglobin and exhaled out of the body.
 
 
 
• **Iron in Haemoglobin**
 
 
• Iron is a critical component of haemoglobin and is necessary for its oxygen-carrying capacity.
 
• Each haemoglobin molecule contains four iron atoms, each capable of binding one oxygen molecule.
 
• Iron deficiency can lead to anaemia, a condition characterized by reduced oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood.
